term: Hello World: How to be Human in the Age of the Machine
definition: Hello World: How to Be Human in the Age of the Machine (also titled Hello World: Being Human in the Age of Algorithms) is a book on the growing influence of algorithms and artificial intelligence (AI) on human life, authored by mathematician and science communicator Hannah Fry.
details: The book examines how algorithms are increasingly shaping decisions in critical areas such as healthcare, transportation, justice, finance, and the arts.

explainer.lead: Hannah Fry’s book explores what happens as algorithms and AI take a larger role in human decisions. Moving across healthcare, transportation, justice, finance, and the arts, it asks how people can remain human in an age shaped by machines.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a machine giving advice about your health, your journey, or a decision in a courtroom. This book asks what happens when machines help make more and more important choices. It explores how people can think carefully about that change and what it means to be human.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers can use the book as a cross-domain prompt for examining the human decisions their systems influence, rather than as an implementation manual. One pitfall is treating algorithms and AI as interchangeable: the book considers the growing influence of both.
tiers.paperLevel: The book addresses the growing influence of algorithms and AI on human life rather than defining a single formal model. Hannah Fry examines decision-making in healthcare, transportation, justice, finance, and the arts. Its central concern is how to be human in the age of the machine.

explainer.example: Consider a justice decision informed by an algorithm. The book treats justice as one domain where growing algorithmic influence prompts broader questions about human judgment and life alongside machines.

explainer.intuition: Algorithms increasingly participate in decisions that affect people, from health and travel to justice and money. Fry’s central question is not only what these systems do, but what their growing influence means for human life.
howItWorks: Identify decisions where algorithms are gaining influence.
Examine those decisions across several areas of human life.
Consider healthcare, transportation, justice, finance, and the arts.
Ask what this machine-shaped world means for being human.
explainer.whyItMatters: The same technological shift touches activities as different as healthcare, transportation, justice, finance, and artistic work. Looking across these domains makes the human consequences of algorithmic decision-making easier to examine.
misconceptions: It is not a programming tutorial based on the usual “Hello, World” coding exercise.
It is not solely about AI; it also examines algorithms more broadly.
